description.narrative: Det övergripande syftet med detta program är att se till att flickor, pojkar och ungdomar i Tanzania skyddas från våld, rustade för att kräva deras rättigheter och tillgång till utbildning i en säker miljö. Detta är ett integrerat program för skydd av barn, barnrättsstyrning och utbildning 2022-2024 för Tanzanias fastland och Zanzibar. Rädda barnen arbetar med nationella och lokala myndigheter (ansvariga för leverans av barns rätt till en säker och rättvis lärandemiljö.

The overall aim of this programme is to ensure girls, boys and youth in Tanzania are protected from violence, equipped to demand their rights, and access education in a safe environment. This is an integrated program on Child protection, Child rights governance and Education 2022-2024 for Tanzania mainland and Zanzibar. Save the children works with the national and local government structures (responsible for delivery of children’s right to safe and equitable learning environment.

The programme approach entails advocating for increased resources/utilization, social mobilization to raise awareness, giving children and young people a voice in policy processes. Overall Goal- Girls, boys and youth in Tanzania are protected from violence, equipped to demand their rights, and access education in a safe environment. Specific Objective: Children are protected and their rights are fulfilled Save the Children will focus on Child Protection, Child Rights Governance and Inclusive Education, and this will be achieved through the following outcomes; Child Protection Outcome 1.1 Girls and boys feel safe within their communities and advocate for their rights Outcome 1.2. Gender dynamics within families are positively influenced and caregivers work to end gender-based violence in their communities Outcome 1.3. Community leaders engaged in work to end sexual violence and protect those who have experienced harm Outcome 1.4. Child protection system and services are strengthened to support girls and boys who have experienced violence. Child rights Governance Outcome 2.1. Civil Society Organizations and child led organizations are capacitated, and able to promote and demand accountability of duty bearers for protection of the rights of girls and boys Outcome 2.2. Girls and boys meaningfully engage through existing platforms to promote their rights and influence decisions Outcome 2.3. Improve capacity and responsiveness of duty-bearers to take children and civil society organisations views into account through child-centered social accountability process. Inclusive Education: Early Childhood Development and Basic Education Outcome 3.1: Improved capacity of LGAs to support holistic child development and pre-primary teaching practices in Mbozi. Outcome 3.2: Strengthened safe learning environment in and around schools in Zanzibar.

During reporting period, the project enhanced childrens ability to raise their voices and engage in advocacy to demand their rights, including gender rights. 74% of the children out of a total of 361 taking part in the annual end line survey reported feeling safe in their communities, as a result of increased interaction between children and parents, a reduction in bullying among children, as well as parents being more aware of Gender Based Violence/Violence Against Children (GBV/VAC) and child rights.
The community leaders at the shehia level Violence Against Women and Children Committees (VAWCC) have identified risks facing children in their communities. These include walking long distances to school with roads that have no bumps and road signs, crossing forest areas and using canoes to get to school which have all contributed to school dropouts and road accidents. Neglect and poverty at home has meant lack of food for children and have led to girls being tempted to engage in sex work, and boys engaging in child labor like selling bungos and coconuts. These risks are now part of the action plans with the shehias committed to work to mitigate the risks by the establishment of bylaws and specific community committees.
In creating spaces for children their voices, SC in collaboration with THRDC, TCRF and the Ministry of Community Development, Gender, Women and Special Group (MoCDGWSG) trained 12 JCURT members on the alternative reporting mechanism for the UNCRC, ACRWC and UPR, where the members reviewed and provided their recommendations on the UNCRC children report. The project has also supported the participation of 60 children in reviewing and providing their recommendations on the Children Act of Zanzibar. Among the issue raised was that the children councils should be included and recognized by the act. Moreover, the project has facilitated 500 children to demand accountability during the advocacy meetings and commemorations of various international days such as DAC and IDGC where children advocated for the end of child marriages and protection from online abuse.
The project enhanced the co-ordination mechanism and systems in delivering quality services within the social welfare, law enforcement, health and the legal sector in supporting girls and boy's survivor of sexual violence. A particular focus was put on children with special needs, including children with disabilities, where SC built the capacity of doctors in conducting forensic investigation and through timely appearance in court hearing sessions. In ensuring sustainability of the One Stop Centre (OSC) services, SC has carried out extensive advocacy work with the Ministry of Health (MoH), who has scaled up the services to ensure access of the service beyond the project coverage by increasing the number of OSCs from 7 to 14 in Zanzibar and budget allocation for human resources.
Additionally, as a result of the education intervention and shown impact in Mbozi, SC successfully engaged in advocacy with the government in the Mbozi district as part of building sustainability, in advocating for increased allocation of resources to support Early Childhood Development (ECD). As a result, during 2023/2024, the government in Mbozi district has committed allocated 96,542,000TZS (408,566 SEK) to support ECD intervention in the district.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
